skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guides an AI coding assistant through final branch checks, integration options, pull request creation, and worktree cleanup after implementation.
skill.summary: Finalize a development branch with tests, Git integration choices, and cleanup safeguards.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and visible shell examples in a Git workflow guide. No prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or hidden execution intent was found, though the documented branch deletion and worktree removal steps should remain clearly gated by user confirmation.

remediation.issue: The worktree detection example uses an unquoted command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Quote the branch lookup and use fixed-string matching so unusual branch names cannot affect grep behavior.

remediation.issue: The discard path documents force deletion and worktree removal.
remediation.suggestion: Keep typed confirmation, show the exact branch and commits, and prefer non-force deletion when possible.

content.value_statement: Development branches often need careful final decisions before merge or cleanup. This skill guides test verification, integration choices, PR creation, and worktree cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Prompts test verification before branch completion decisions.
Helps identify a likely base branch with Git merge-base checks.
Presents four completion choices for merge, pull request, keep, or discard.
Documents steps for local merge, pull request creation, branch deletion, and worktree cleanup.
Requires typed confirmation before destructive discard actions.
Lists common mistakes and red flags for branch completion.
limitations: It depends on the connected assistant to run tests and Git commands correctly.
It assumes Git is available, and the pull request path assumes GitHub CLI access.
It uses generic test command placeholders that must match each project.
Destructive cleanup still requires users to verify branch names, commits, and paths.

use_cases.title: Complete a Solo Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Verify tests, choose a merge or keep path, and clean up local branch state after implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Team Pull Request
use_cases.description: Push a completed branch, draft a concise pull request summary, and preserve the worktree for review changes.

use_cases.title: Close Worktree-Based Tasks
use_cases.description: Finish a task branch created in a separate worktree and remove local worktree state only when appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Branch Finish
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a small implementation is complete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to help me finish my current development branch. Verify tests first, then present the standard completion options.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Integration Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need help deciding between merge, PR, keep, or discard.
prompt_templates.prompt: I finished implementation on a feature branch. Use the finishing-a-development-branch workflow and help me choose the right integration path.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Completion Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the assistant can inspect the repository and run commands.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the branch completion workflow for this repository. Identify the base branch, verify tests, present the four options, and wait for my choice.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Pull Request Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a reviewed pull request is likely but not final.
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete this worktree-based branch using the skill. After tests pass, prepare the pull request path with a concise summary and test plan.

output_examples.input: Implementation is complete, and I need to decide what happens to the branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies tests, identifies the base branch, and presents four choices: merge locally, create a pull request, keep the branch, or discard.

output_examples.input: I want to create a pull request after finishing the work.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a branch push and pull request draft with a summary and test plan, then keeps the worktree for review updates.

output_examples.input: This branch should be discarded after testing.
output_examples.output: The assistant shows the affected branch, commits, and worktree path, then waits for typed discard confirmation before cleanup.

best_practices: Run the real project test command before choosing any completion option.
Review the branch name, base branch, commits, and worktree path before cleanup.
Use the pull request path when team review or CI validation is required.
anti_patterns: Do not merge or push when tests are failing.
Do not delete branches or worktrees without explicit user confirmation.
Do not replace the four clear options with an open-ended question.

faq.question: Does this skill merge automatically?
faq.answer: No. It directs the assistant to verify tests, present options, and wait for your choice before integration steps.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a GitHub CLI workflow for pushing a branch and preparing a pull request body.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: Only the pull request option assumes GitHub CLI. Local merge and branch cleanup use Git.

faq.question: How does it prevent accidental deletion?
faq.answer: It requires typed discard confirmation and lists the affected branch, commits, and worktree before deletion.

faq.question: What tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for Git worktrees?
faq.answer: It includes worktree cleanup guidance, but users should verify the worktree path before removal.
